mainTopic: Forgotten additions in ברכת המזון and תפלה, the minimum amount for זימון, and the wording of זימון by group size
overview: The amud opens in the middle of a story. רב נחמן forgot to mention שבת in ברכת המזון and went back to the beginning. Based on two rulings of רב, the rule is: if you have not yet started 'הטוב והמטיב', you add 'ברוך שנתן'; once you have started it, you restart. שמואל rules that forgetting ראש חודש requires repeating תפלה but not ברכת המזון. רב נחמן explains why: תפלה is a fixed obligation, while eating on ראש חודש is optional. On שבת and יום טוב, when eating is required, one does go back. Next the גמרא asks how much food makes a person part of a זימון, and settles an apparent contradiction between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה (כזית vs. כביצה) in two ways: רבי יוחנן switches the names, and אביי says one argument comes from a פסוק and the other from logic. A new משנה lists how the זימון wording grows with the size of the group, with a dispute between רבי יוסי הגלילי, רבי עקיבא and רבי ישמעאל. The גמרא then brings שמואל's rule never to exclude yourself from the group, challenges it from the משנה's 'ברכו', and begins a new reading of the משנה that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב נחמן goes back, and גידל asks why
steps.stepSummary: The story continues: רב נחמן made a mistake in ברכת המזון and went back to the beginning. גידל בר מניומי asks him why he did that.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he went back to the beginning. גידל said to him: Why did the master do that?
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of a story. רב נחמן forgot to mention שבת in ברכת המזון and restarted the whole ברכת המזון, and his student asks him for the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Restarting the whole ברכת המזון is a big step, so the student wants the source. This question sets up the debate in the next steps about when restarting is required.

keyTerms.meaning: He went back to the beginning
What is the reason?
Master (a respectful way to address a rabbi)

phrases.english: And he returned to the beginning.
phrases.notes: רב נחמן restarted ברכת המזון after forgetting שבת.

phrases.english: He (Giddel bar Manyumi) said to him: What is the reason
that the master acted this way?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי טַעְמָא עָבֵיד מָר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story begun on the previous amud (רב נחמן forgot שבת in ברכת המזון).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for restarting ברכת המזון after forgetting to mention שבת.

steps.title: רב נחמן's source: one who errs goes back to the start
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers by quoting רבי שילא in the name of רב: if you made a mistake, you return to the beginning.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Because רבי שילא said in the name of רב: If he erred, he returns to the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן explains that he was following a ruling of רב, which says to restart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is short and general: a mistake means restarting. Because it is so short, the next step will show it seems to clash with another quote from the same רב.

keyTerms.meaning: He erred / made a mistake
He returns to the beginning

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שֵׁילָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: He said to him: Because Rabbi Sheila said that Rav said:
If one erred, he returns to the beginning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב ruled (via רבי שילא) that one who erred returns to the beginning of ברכת המזון.

steps.title: Challenge: רב also said to just add 'ברוך שנתן'
steps.stepSummary: גידל challenges: רב הונא quoted רב as saying that one who erred just says a short extra blessing, 'ברוך שנתן', and does not restart.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב הונא say in the name of רב: If he erred, he says 'Blessed is He Who gave'?
steps.whatsHappening: The student pushes back. He quotes a different ruling from the same רב that seems to say you do not need to restart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two students of רב report two different rulings: restart, or add a short blessing ('ברוך שנתן שבתות למנוחה'). The challenge is that רב seems to contradict himself, so why did רב נחמן restart?

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that... (opens a challenge)
'Blessed is He Who gave' (the short added blessing for שבת)

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Huna say that Rav said:
If one erred, he says 'Blessed is He Who gave'!
phrases.notes: A short blessing added in place of the missing mention, with no need to restart.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source cited in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's practice of restarting, based on רבי שילא's report of רב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another report of רב says one only adds 'ברוך שנתן', so restarting seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Resolution: it depends on whether you started 'הטוב והמטיב'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that רב's ruling was explained: the short blessing works only if you have not begun the fourth blessing, 'הטוב והמטיב'. If you already began it, you restart.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Wasn't it said about this, by רב מנשיא בר תחליפא in the name of רב: They only taught this when he had not yet begun 'Who is good and does good'. But if he had begun 'Who is good and does good', he returns to the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן shows that the two rulings of רב fit together, because each one is for a different stage of the mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you catch the mistake before starting 'הטוב והמטיב', you add 'ברוך שנתן' right there. Once you have started 'הטוב והמטיב', it is too late for the short fix, so you restart. This tells us רב נחמן had already begun 'הטוב והמטיב'.

keyTerms.meaning: Wasn't it stated about this? (introduces a clarification of the ruling)
They only taught this in the case of...
He began
'Who is good and does good', the fourth blessing of ברכת המזון

steps.whatToRemember: Forgot שבת in ברכת המזון: before starting 'הטוב והמטיב', add 'ברוך שנתן'. After starting 'הטוב והמטיב', go back to the beginning.

phrases.english: He said to him: Wasn't it stated about this,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב מְנַשְּׁיָא בַּר תַּחְלִיפָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Menashya bar Tachlifa said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא פָּתַח בְּ״הַטּוֹב וְהַמֵּטִיב״,
phrases.english: They only taught this where he did not yet begin 'Who is good and does good',
but if he began 'Who is good and does good',
he returns to the beginning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: the two rulings apply at different stages of the mistake.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's two rulings contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ברוך שנתן' applies before 'הטוב והמטיב'. Restarting applies after one began 'הטוב והמטיב'.

steps.title: שמואל: forgetting ראש חודש in תפלה vs. ברכת המזון
steps.stepSummary: Through a chain of names, שמואל rules: forgetting ראש חודש in תפלה means you repeat it, but forgetting it in ברכת המזון does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אידי בר אבין said that רב עמרם said that רב נחמן said that שמואל said: If one erred and did not mention ראש חודש in the תפלה, we make him go back. In ברכת המזון, we do not make him go back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new, related ruling about forgetting ראש חודש. It treats תפלה and ברכת המזון differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic shifts from שבת to ראש חודש. The same mistake gets two different results: in תפלה you repeat, and in ברכת המזון you do not. That difference will be questioned next.

keyTerms.meaning: The New Month
The שמונה עשרה / עמידה prayer
We make him go back and repeat
Grace after meals

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב עַמְרָם
phrases.english: Rav Idi bar Avin said that Rav Amram said
that Rav Nachman said that Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: טָעָה וְלֹא הִזְכִּיר שֶׁל רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ בַּתְּפִלָּה —
phrases.english: If one erred and did not mention Rosh Chodesh in the Tefillah,
we make him go back.
In Birkas HaMazon, we do not make him go back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב עַמְרָם אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, related ruling about forgotten additions, now about ראש חודש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Forgetting ראש חודש: in תפלה we make him repeat. In ברכת המזון we do not.

steps.title: רב אבין asks: why the difference?
steps.stepSummary: רב אבין asks רב עמרם why תפלה and ברכת המזון are treated differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אבין said to רב עמרם: What is different about תפלה, and what is different about ברכת המזון?
steps.whatsHappening: Someone asks for the reasoning behind שמואל's split ruling. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both are blessings with a ראש חודש addition, so why repeat one and not the other? The question asks for the logic, not a source.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? (asks for the reason behind a distinction)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָבִין לְרַב עַמְרָם:
phrases.english: Rav Avin said to Rav Amram:
What is different about Tefillah
and what is different about Birkas HaMazon?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא תְּפִלָּה וּמַאי שְׁנָא בִּרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the distinction made in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason תפלה requires repetition but ברכת המזון does not.

steps.title: תפלה is an obligation; eating is optional
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם says he had the same question and asked רב נחמן. רב נחמן did not hear a reason from שמואל, but he reasoned: תפלה is a fixed obligation, so you repeat it. ברכת המזון depends on whether you chose to eat, so you do not repeat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This was difficult for me too, and I asked רב נחמן. He said to me: I did not hear it from מר שמואל, but let us figure it out ourselves. תפלה is an obligation, so we make him go back. ברכת המזון depends on eating, and if he wants he eats and if he wants he does not eat, so we do not make him go back.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן admits he has no tradition for the reason, so he works it out himself: an obligation is repeated, but something you only took on by choosing to eat is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You must daven every day no matter what, so a flawed תפלה is redone. ברכת המזון comes only because you chose to eat, and nobody must eat bread on ראש חודש, so the ראש חודש mention there is not strict enough to require repeating.

keyTerms.meaning: It was difficult for me too
I did not hear it (I have no tradition)
Let us see / figure it out ourselves
An obligation
If he wants

steps.whatToRemember: Forgetting ראש חודש: in תפלה (a fixed חובה) you repeat. In ברכת המזון (which depends on choosing to eat) you do not repeat.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the שבת case in steps 1–4, where רב נחמן did restart ברכת המזון. The logic here explains the difference: on ראש חודש eating is optional, but on שבת and יום טוב eating a meal is required, so a missed mention there is treated more strictly. The גמרא itself makes this point in steps 8–9.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key rule for the halacha of forgotten additions: whether you must repeat depends on whether the underlying act is a fixed obligation or something you chose to do.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַף לְדִידִי קַשְׁיָא לִי
phrases.english: He said to him: It was difficult for me too,
and I asked Rav Nachman about it, and he said to me:

phrases.aramaic: מִינֵּיהּ דְּמָר שְׁמוּאֵל לָא שְׁמִיעַ לִי,
phrases.english: From Mar Shmuel himself I did not hear it,
but let us see for ourselves:
Tefillah, which is an obligation, we make him go back.
Birkas HaMazon, where if he wants he eats,
and if he wants he does not eat,
we do not make him go back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא נֶחְזֵי אֲנַן: תְּפִלָּה דְּחוֹבָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: תפלה is a fixed obligation, so it is repeated. ברכת המזון depends on optional eating, so it is not repeated.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether a forgotten ראש חודש mention requires repeating depends on whether the underlying act is obligatory (תפלה) or chosen (eating, and so ברכת המזון).

steps.title: What about שבת and יום טוב, when eating is required?
steps.stepSummary: If ברכת המזון is not repeated because eating is optional, then on שבת and יום טוב, when eating is required, should one go back and repeat it?
steps.simpleTranslation: But if that is the reason, then on שבתות and ימים טובים, when a person must eat, should he also go back and repeat ברכת המזון if he forgets?
steps.whatsHappening: The questioner takes רב נחמן's reason from step 7 and tests it on a new case: שבת and יום טוב, when a person is required to eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן said ברכת המזון is not repeated because you did not have to eat. On שבת and יום טוב you do have to eat, so by his own logic you should have to repeat it. The questioner asks whether this really follows, and the next step answers that it does.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so / if that is your reasoning (introduces an unwanted result of an argument)
שבתות and ימים טובים (Festivals)
It is impossible not to (there is no way to avoid)
He goes back (repeats)

phrases.english: But now, if that is so,
Shabbatot and Festivals,
when it is not possible for him not to eat,
phrases.notes: There is a requirement to eat a meal on these days.

phrases.english: would it also be that if he errs, he goes back?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רב נחמן's reasoning from step 7 to a new case to see whether it leads to an unwanted result.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's reasoning that ברכת המזון is not repeated because eating is optional.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: On שבת and יום טוב eating is required. So by that reasoning, forgetting there should require repeating ברכת המזון, which seems like a strange result.

steps.title: Yes, on שבת and יום טוב you restart
steps.stepSummary: The answer accepts the result: yes, on שבת and יום טוב one who forgets goes back to the beginning, as רבי שילא taught in the name of רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes. As רבי שילא said in the name of רב: If he made a mistake, he goes back to the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of avoiding the result, the answer says yes: on שבת and יום טוב you really do go back and repeat ברכת המזון. It brings support from רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What looked like a problem is actually the correct ruling. Since the meal is required on these days, forgetting the addition means you start ברכת המזון again. This fits רב נחמן's reasoning perfectly.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
He made a mistake / he forgot
He goes back to the beginning

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes,
as Rabbi Sheila said that Rav said:
If he erred, he returns to the beginning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the result raised in step 8 and supports it with a teaching from רב.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. On שבת and יום טוב one who forgets the addition in ברכת המזון goes back to the beginning, as רבי שילא taught in the name of רב.

steps.title: But רב also said to say 'ברוך שנתן'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: רב הונא quoted רב as saying that one who forgets just says the short blessing 'ברוך שנתן' and does not restart.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב הונא said in the name of רב: If he made a mistake, he says 'ברוך שנתן' (Blessed is He Who gave)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רב can say 'go back to the beginning' when another student quoted him as saying 'just add a short blessing'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two reports from רב that seem to clash: רבי שילא says you restart, and רב הונא says you only add 'ברוך שנתן'. This is the same challenge גידל raised in step 3, and the גמרא repeats it here because it now matters for proving the ruling about שבת and יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely (introduces a contradicting source)
'Blessed is He Who gave' — a short extra blessing for the day, said instead of restarting

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an accidental repeat. The גמרא itself repeats the challenge and answer from steps 3–4, because here they are needed to defend רבי שילא's report.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Huna say that Rav said:
If he erred, he says 'Blessed is He Who gave'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source quoted in step 9 with a contradicting report from רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שילא's report in the name of רב that one who forgets goes back to the beginning.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב הונא reports that רב said one only adds 'ברוך שנתן' and does not restart, so רב seems to contradict himself.

steps.title: The short blessing works only before 'הטוב והמטיב'
steps.stepSummary: The answer: רב's ruling about 'ברוך שנתן' applies only if you have not started 'הטוב והמטיב'. Once you have started it, you go back to the beginning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wasn't it said about that ruling: They only taught this when he did not yet begin 'הטוב והמטיב'. But if he began 'הטוב והמטיב', he goes back to the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the clash by showing that the two reports from רב are talking about two different moments in ברכת המזון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the fourth blessing ('הטוב והמטיב'), you can fix the mistake by adding 'ברוך שנתן'. After you begin it, that fix is no longer available, so you restart. רבי שילא's report speaks about the later case, so there is no contradiction, and the ruling that שבת and יום טוב require repeating stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated about it (an explanation attached to an earlier ruling)
They only taught this in the case of (narrows a ruling)
'Who is good and does good' — the fourth blessing of ברכת המזון

steps.whatToRemember: On שבת and יום טוב, if you forget the addition in ברכת המזון: before you start 'הטוב והמטיב', add 'ברוך שנתן'. After you start it, go back to the beginning. On ראש חודש you do not go back at all.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical rule for forgetting רצה or יעלה ויבוא on שבת and יום טוב, based on the difference between a required meal and an optional one.

phrases.english: Wasn't it stated about it:
They only taught this
when he did not begin 'Who is good and does good,'
but if he began 'Who is good and does good,'
he returns to the beginning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 by limiting רב הונא's report to an earlier point in ברכת המזון.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא by timing): each report from רב applies to a different stage of ברכת המזון.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב said 'ברוך שנתן' is always enough, which would contradict 'חוזר לראש'.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ברוך שנתן' works only before starting 'הטוב והמטיב'. After that, one goes back to the beginning, so both reports of רב are true.

steps.title: New topic: How much food is needed for a זימון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: how much must one eat to be counted for זימון?
steps.simpleTranslation: Up to how much do they make a זימון, etc. (the משנה: an olive-bulk; רבי יהודה says an egg-bulk).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting the opening words of the next line in the משנה. It is setting up a question about this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that eating a כזית is enough to join a זימון (this is רבי מאיר's view), while רבי יהודה requires a כביצה. The 'וכו׳' tells us to remember the rest of the משנה, which is what the next step will discuss.

keyTerms.meaning: They join together for זימון (the group invitation to ברכת המזון)
Etc. — the rest of the quoted line is assumed
An olive-bulk (a small minimum amount of food)

phrases.english: Up to how much [food] do they join for zimmun, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה continues: a כזית; רבי יהודה says a כביצה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the ברכת המזון discussion and begins a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's dispute: the first view (רבי מאיר) says a כזית is enough for זימון, and רבי יהודה says a כביצה is needed.

steps.title: Don't רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה hold the opposite elsewhere?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: does this mean רבי מאיר considers a כזית important and רבי יהודה a כביצה? Elsewhere we heard them say the reverse!
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say that רבי מאיר considers a כזית important, and רבי יהודה a כביצה? But we heard them say the opposite!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction. In our משנה, רבי מאיר uses the smaller amount and רבי יהודה the bigger one, but in another place they seem to switch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each sage should be consistent about what amount of food counts as 'important'. Here רבי מאיר says כזית and רבי יהודה says כביצה. The גמרא is about to quote a source where רבי מאיר says כביצה and רבי יהודה says כזית.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? (draws a conclusion in order to question it)
Considers important / significant
The opposite / reversed
We heard them (say)

phrases.english: Is that to say that Rabbi Meir
considers an olive-bulk significant,
and Rabbi Yehuda an egg-bulk?
But we heard them say the opposite!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר חָשֵׁיב לֵיהּ כְּזַיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the positions in the משנה just quoted by pointing out a contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The positions of רבי מאיר (כזית) and רבי יהודה (כביצה) in the זימון משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In another משנה, the two sages hold the reverse amounts, so each one seems to contradict himself.

steps.title: The source: someone who leaves Jerusalem holding holy meat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting the contradicting משנה: a person who left ירושלים with holy meat burns it where he is if he passed צופים. If not, he goes back and burns it in front of the Temple.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: Similarly, one who left ירושלים and remembered he had holy meat in his hand: if he already passed צופים, he burns it where he is. If not, he goes back and burns it in front of the בירה (the Temple) with wood from the altar pile.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting the other משנה that it will use to show the contradiction. This part sets up the case. The amounts come in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Holy meat may not leave ירושלים, so it becomes unfit and must be burned. If he is already far away (past צופים), he burns it on the spot. If he is still close, he must go back and burn it at the Temple. The word 'וכן' (similarly) connects this to an earlier case in that משנה about חמץ, which is why the next step says 'this and that'.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy meat from a sacrifice
Mount Scopus, the last point on the road from which the Temple can still be seen. Past it, one no longer has to go back.
The Temple (literally 'the fortress / capital')
Wood of the altar pile, used to burn disqualified holy items

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
And similarly, one who left Jerusalem
phrases.notes: 'Similarly' refers back to the earlier case in that משנה, about someone who remembered he had חמץ at home.

phrases.english: and remembered that he had holy meat in his hand,
if he passed Mount Scopus,
he burns it where he is;
and if not, he goes back
and burns it in front of the Temple
with the wood of the altar pile.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source text behind the contradiction claimed in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה hold the reverse amounts elsewhere.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה (in פסחים) about one who left ירושלים with holy meat.

steps.title: In that source, רבי מאיר says כביצה and רבי יהודה says כזית
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: how much meat (or חמץ) requires going back? רבי מאיר says a כביצה, and רבי יהודה says a כזית, which is the reverse of their views on זימון.
steps.simpleTranslation: For how much must they go back? רבי מאיר says: for both this and that, a כביצה. רבי יהודה says: for both this and that, a כזית.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the punchline of the contradiction. In this משנה, רבי מאיר requires the bigger amount and רבי יהודה the smaller one, the opposite of the זימון משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the זימון משנה, רבי מאיר treats a כזית as important and רבי יהודה needs a כביצה. Here רבי מאיר needs a כביצה before it is worth going back, while רבי יהודה says even a כזית is enough. So each sage appears to contradict himself, and the גמרא will need to resolve this.

keyTerms.meaning: This and that — here, both the holy meat and the חמץ
An egg-bulk (a larger amount than a כזית)
They go back

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two sources. In זימון: רבי מאיר = כזית and רבי יהודה = כביצה. In the holy meat case: רבי מאיר = כביצה and רבי יהודה = כזית. That reversal is the whole problem.

phrases.english: For how much must they go back?
Rabbi Meir says:
For this and that, an egg-bulk.
And Rabbi Yehuda says:
For this and that, an olive-bulk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quoted משנה and shows the reversed amounts that create the contradiction.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה hold reversed amounts compared to the זימון משנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The second half of the משנה about returning to burn holy meat and חמץ: רבי מאיר says כביצה, רבי יהודה says כזית.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the names are switched
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן fixes the contradiction by saying the names of רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה are switched in one of the two sources.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: the opinions are reversed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer to the contradiction: רבי יוחנן says one of the two sources has the opinions written under the wrong names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In זימון, רבי מאיר says a כזית and רבי יהודה says a כביצה, but for bringing back holy meat their views are the opposite. רבי יוחנן's answer is to fix the text by swapping the names in one place. After that, each רבי is consistent in both places.

keyTerms.meaning: Reversed, switched
The line of opinions, meaning which name goes with which view

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
The opinions are reversed.
phrases.notes: One of the two sources must be fixed by swapping the names.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 13 and laid out in steps 14-15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Fixing the text (swapping which name goes with which view)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה contradict themselves on כזית vs. כביצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The names are switched in one source, so each רבי really holds one consistent view.

steps.title: אביי: for זימון they argue about how to read a verse
steps.stepSummary: אביי says not to switch anything. For זימון, the argument comes from reading the פסוק 'ואכלת ושבעת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: actually, do not reverse anything. Here they argue about verses. רבי מאיר holds: 'and you shall eat' means eating, 'and be satisfied' means drinking, and eating is a כזית. רבי יהודה holds: 'and you shall eat and be satisfied' means eating that makes you full, and that is a כביצה.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a different answer: keep the text as it is, because the two arguments come from different reasons. Here he explains the reason behind the argument about זימון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר splits the פסוק in two. 'ואכלת' is eating, which is always a כזית, and 'ושבעת' refers to drinking. רבי יהודה reads the words together as one idea: eating that satisfies, which needs a כביצה. So their positions on זימון come from reading a פסוק, not from a general rule about measurements.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, do not reverse it
Verses (פסוקים)
'And you shall eat and be satisfied', the פסוק for ברכת המזון
Satisfaction, being full
The size of an egg

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying the two רבנן changed their minds. He is saying the two arguments have different sources (a פסוק here, logic there), so there was never a real contradiction.

phrases.english: Abaye said: actually, do not reverse it.
Here (by zimmun), they disagree about verses.
Rabbi Meir holds:
'And you shall eat': this is eating,
'and be satisfied': this is drinking,
and eating is with an olive-bulk.
And Rabbi Yehuda holds:
'And you shall eat and be satisfied' means
eating that has satisfaction in it,
and which amount is that? An egg-bulk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the contradiction, instead of רבי יוחנן's fix in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different reasons in different topics (a פסוק vs. logic)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two arguments are about the same thing, so the רבנן's positions should match in both.
steps.terutzMaskana: For זימון the argument comes from reading 'ואכלת ושבעת', so it does not have to match the holy-meat case.

steps.title: אביי: for returning holy meat they argue from logic
steps.stepSummary: אביי finishes his answer. For bringing back holy meat, רבי מאיר compares it to the measure for טומאה (כביצה), and רבי יהודה compares it to the measure for the איסור (כזית).
steps.simpleTranslation: There, they disagree from logic. רבי מאיר holds: returning it is like its impurity. Just as its impurity is with a כביצה, so its returning is with a כביצה. רבי יהודה holds: returning it is like its prohibition. Just as its prohibition is with a כזית, so its returning is with a כזית.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his answer by explaining the reason behind the argument about bringing back holy meat (and חמץ). This argument comes from logic, not from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food becomes טמא only if it is at least a כביצה, so רבי מאיר links the duty to go back to that measure. Eating something forbidden is only counted with a כזית, so רבי יהודה links the duty to go back to that measure. Since the reasons here have nothing to do with the פסוק about זימון, the two arguments do not contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: There, meaning in the other source
Logical reasoning
Its returning, the duty to go back with it
Its becoming ritually impure
Its prohibition (the איסור to eat it)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to the contradiction. רבי יוחנן switches the names. אביי keeps the text, because the זימון argument comes from a פסוק and the holy-meat argument comes from logic.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common way the גמרא settles a contradiction: the same רבי can use different measurements in different topics when each topic has its own reason.

phrases.english: There (by holy meat), they disagree based on logic.
Rabbi Meir holds:
its returning is like its impurity.
Just as its impurity is with an egg-bulk,
so too its returning is with an egg-bulk.
And Rabbi Yehuda holds:
its returning is like its prohibition.
Just as its prohibition is with an olive-bulk,
so too its returning is with an olive-bulk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes אביי's answer from step 17 by explaining the other side of the contradiction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different reasons in different topics (completing אביי's answer)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The measure for going back with holy meat should match the measure for זימון.
steps.terutzMaskana: Going back with holy meat is measured by comparing it to טומאה or to the איסור, which has nothing to do with the זימון פסוק.

steps.title: משנה: זימון wording with three people
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins: with three people the leader says 'נברך'; with three people plus himself he says 'ברכו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: How do we make a זימון? With three, he says 'Let us bless.' With three and himself, he says 'Bless.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It teaches how the words of the זימון change depending on how many people ate together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When there are exactly three, the leader is needed to make the group, so he includes himself: 'נברך' (let us bless). When there are three others besides him, the group exists without him, so he can speak to them: 'ברכו' (bless).

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (short for מתניתין)
How do we make a זימון?
Let us bless
Bless! (said to the others)

steps.confusionAlert: 'בשלשה והוא' means three people plus the leader, which is four in total. It does not mean the leader is one of the three.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
How do we make a zimmun?
With three, he says: 'Let us bless.'
With three and himself, he says: 'Bless.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion has ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With three, the leader says 'נברך'. With three plus himself, he says 'ברכו'.

steps.title: משנה: זימון wording with ten people and more
steps.stepSummary: With ten people, God's name is added: 'נברך אלהינו'. With ten plus himself, the leader says 'ברכו'. The wording is the same for ten and for a hundred thousand.
steps.simpleTranslation: With ten, he says 'Let us bless our God.' With ten and himself, he says 'Bless.' Ten and a hundred thousand are the same.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues. With ten people, the זימון adds the word אלהינו, and the words stay the same no matter how much bigger the group gets.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once there are ten (a מנין), God's name is mentioned in the זימון. The same rule from before applies: if the leader is needed to make the ten, he says 'let us bless'; if there are ten without him, he says 'bless'. According to this משנה, a group of a hundred thousand uses the same words as ten.

keyTerms.meaning: Our God, added once there are ten
Ten people, a מנין
Ten thousand (so עשרה רבוא is a hundred thousand)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next part of the משנה and גמרא, which discuss whether the wording keeps changing as the group gets larger.

phrases.english: With ten, he says: 'Let us bless our God.'
With ten and himself, he says: 'Bless.'
The same for ten and for a hundred thousand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from step 19, moving from three people to ten.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With ten, אלהינו is added ('נברך אלהינו', or 'ברכו' if there are ten besides him), and the wording is the same up to a hundred thousand.

steps.title: Wording for one hundred and for one thousand people
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues its list. With one hundred people the leader adds God's name 'ה׳'. With one thousand people he also adds 'אלהי ישראל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: With one hundred people, the leader says 'Let us bless ה׳ our God.' With one hundred plus himself, he says 'Bless.' With one thousand people, he says 'Let us bless ה׳ our God, the God of Israel.' With one thousand plus himself, he says 'Bless.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps going up the ladder of group sizes. Each bigger group adds more words of praise to the invitation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At ten people the leader said 'אלהינו'. At one hundred he adds the name ה׳, and at one thousand he adds 'אלהי ישראל'. The rule from step 19 stays the same: when the leader is not counted in the round number, he says 'ברכו' and not 'נברך'.

keyTerms.meaning: One hundred
One thousand
'And him', meaning the group plus the leader himself
The God of Israel, a praise added at one thousand people

steps.confusionAlert: Step 20 said the wording is the same for ten and for a huge crowd. This step gives a different wording for each size. These look like two different opinions inside the משנה. The disagreement between רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא (steps 24–25) points to who holds which view, and the גמרא takes this up on the next amud.

phrases.english: With one hundred, he says:
'Let us bless the Lord our God,'
with one hundred and him, he says 'Bless.'
phrases.notes: He says 'Bless' together with the full wording for that group size.

phrases.english: And with one thousand, he says:
'Let us bless the Lord our God, the God of Israel,'
with one thousand and him, he says 'Bless.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of זימון wordings, moving up from ten people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With 100 people the leader adds ה׳. With 1,000 people he also adds אלהי ישראל. When the group is that number plus the leader, he says ברכו.

steps.title: Wording for ten thousand people
steps.stepSummary: For the largest group, ten thousand, the leader uses the fullest wording. He adds 'אלהי צבאות יושב הכרובים' and 'על המזון שאכלנו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: With ten thousand people, the leader says: 'Let us bless ה׳ our God, the God of Israel, the God of Hosts, Who sits upon the כרובים, for the food that we have eaten.' With ten thousand plus himself, he says 'Bless.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה reaches the top of the ladder. The biggest group gets the longest and fullest invitation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two more praises are added here: 'the God of Hosts' and 'Who sits upon the כרובים'. The phrase 'for the food that we have eaten' also appears, which ties the praise back to the meal. The same 'ברכו' rule applies when the leader is not counted in the number.

keyTerms.meaning: Ten thousand
The God of Hosts
Who sits upon the כרובים, the golden angel figures on the ארון
For the food that we have eaten

phrases.english: With ten thousand, he says:
'Let us bless the Lord our God, the God of Israel,
the God of Hosts, Who sits upon the cherubs,
for the food that we have eaten,'
with ten thousand and him, he says 'Bless.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ladder of group sizes with the largest group.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With 10,000 people the leader uses the full wording, ending 'על המזון שאכלנו'.

steps.title: The group answers with the same wording
steps.stepSummary: Whatever wording the leader uses, the people answer with that same wording, beginning with 'ברוך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as the leader blesses, so the people answer after him: 'Blessed is ה׳ our God, the God of Israel, the God of Hosts, Who sits upon the כרובים, for the food that we have eaten.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells us how the group responds. Their answer matches the leader's invitation word for word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The leader invites with 'נברך' or 'ברכו'. The group answers with 'ברוך' plus the same praises he used. The example shown is the fullest version, the one for ten thousand people.

keyTerms.meaning: In the same manner
They answer after him
Blessed is, the opening word of the group's response

phrases.english: In the same manner that he blesses,
so they answer after him:
'Blessed is the Lord our God, the God of Israel,
the God of Hosts, Who sits upon the cherubs,
for the food that we have eaten.'

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּעִנְיָן שֶׁהוּא מְבָרֵךְ, כָּךְ עוֹנִים אַחֲרָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the group's response to the leader's invitation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The group answers 'ברוך' using the same praises the leader used.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי: the wording follows the size of the crowd
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי holds that the blessing changes with the size of the gathering. He brings a פסוק from תהלים as his source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי הגלילי says: they bless according to the size of the crowd, as it says, 'In assemblies bless God, ה׳, you who are from the source of Israel.'
steps.whatsHappening: A named תנא gives the source for growing the wording with the crowd. He learns it from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'במקהלות', in assemblies, teaches that the size of the gathering affects how God is blessed. A bigger crowd brings more honor to God, so more praise is said. This supports the ladder of wordings we just learned.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the size of the crowd
In assemblies (תהלים סח:כז)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
according to the size of the crowd they bless,
as it is stated: 'In assemblies bless God,
the Lord, you who are from the source of Israel.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר: לְפִי רוֹב הַקָּהָל הֵם מְבָרְכִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a named author and a פסוק for the idea that the wording grows with the crowd.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wording of the blessing depends on the size of the gathering, based on 'במקהלות'.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the size of the crowd makes no difference
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא disagrees. He compares זימון to the בית הכנסת, where the same 'ברכו את ה׳' is said whether the crowd is large or small.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said: What do we find in the בית הכנסת? Whether there are many people or few, the leader says 'Bless ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives the opposite view. He proves it from what is done in the בית הכנסת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the בית הכנסת, once there is a מנין, the leader always says 'ברכו את ה׳'. It does not matter how many people are there. רבי עקיבא learns זימון from that practice, so for him there is no ladder of wordings above ten.

keyTerms.meaning: What do we find? Used to bring a comparison from a known case
Synagogue
Many people
Few people

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said:
what do we find in the synagogue?
whether many or few,
he says 'Bless the Lord.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: מַה מָּצִינוּ בְּבֵית הַכְּנֶסֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יוסי הגלילי and holds that crowd size does not change the wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The size of the crowd does not change the wording. We learn this from the בית הכנסת.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: add the word המבורך
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל holds that the בית הכנסת wording is 'ברכו את ה׳ המבורך', with the word 'המבורך' added.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: the leader says 'Bless ה׳, the Blessed One.'
steps.whatsHappening: A third תנא argues about the exact words said in the בית הכנסת. He adds 'המבורך'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל agrees there is one fixed call, but he adds 'המבורך', the Blessed One. This is the wording we use today for ברכו in davening. Adding the word keeps the leader from seeming to bless only others while leaving himself out.

keyTerms.meaning: The Blessed One

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the wording 'ברכו את ה׳ המבורך' that we say in davening today.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael says:
'Bless the Lord, the Blessed One.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues with רבי עקיבא about the exact wording of the call.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The call is 'ברכו את ה׳ המבורך'.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three views in the משנה. רבי יוסי הגלילי says the wording grows with the crowd. רבי עקיבא says it stays the same like in the בית הכנסת. רבי ישמעאל says the wording is 'ברכו את ה׳ המבורך'.

steps.title: The גמרא opens: never exclude yourself from the group
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins with שמואל's rule that a person should never separate himself from the community.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: שמואל said: A person should never take himself out of the group.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of this משנה with a general rule from שמואל. It is setting up the next move, because this rule seems to clash with the משנה's instruction to say 'ברכו'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'ברכו' (you bless) sounds as if the leader leaves himself out. Saying 'נברך' (let us bless) includes him. שמואל's rule leans toward always including oneself, so the גמרא will next need to check it against the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Always, never (with 'אל')
A person should not take himself out
From the group, the community

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל is not just giving good advice about community life. In this context, his rule is about the wording of זימון: 'נברך' includes the leader, while 'ברכו' seems to leave him out.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Shmuel said:
a person should never exclude
himself from the collective.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: לְעוֹלָם אַל יוֹצִיא אָדָם אֶת עַצְמוֹ מִן הַכְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא on the משנה with a rule that bears on the 'נברך' versus 'ברכו' wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should never exclude himself from the group, which points toward the leader saying 'נברך'.

steps.title: Our משנה seems to have the leader leave himself out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל from our משנה. It says that with 'three and him,' the leader says 'ברכו,' a word that seems to leave him out of the group.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in our משנה: when there are three people and him, he says 'ברכו' ('You bless')!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes our own משנה to attack שמואל's rule. The משנה seems to show the leader using wording that separates him from the group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said a person should never take himself out of the group. That means he should say 'נברך' ('Let us bless'), which includes himself. But the משנה says that with 'three and him' the leader says 'ברכו' ('You bless'). That wording speaks only to the others, so the משנה seems to go against שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: With three people and him. This means three others plus the leader.
'You bless.' Here the leader speaks to the others and does not include himself.
'Let us bless.' This wording includes the speaker in the group.

steps.confusionAlert: 'בשלשה והוא' does not mean three people in total. It means three people plus the leader.

phrases.english: We learned: with three and him —
phrases.notes: The quote comes from our own משנה.

phrases.english: he says 'Bless' (you bless)!
phrases.notes: The exclamation mark shows this is a challenge: the wording seems to leave the leader out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks שמואל's rule from Step 27 using our משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that a person should never separate himself from the group.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה has the leader say 'ברכו,' which leaves him out of the group. This seems to contradict שמואל, who requires wording that includes himself.

steps.title: Opening of the answer: read the משנה differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer with 'אימא' ('Say'). This signals that the משנה should be read in a different way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead that the משנה means:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is starting its answer and getting ready to explain the משנה in a way that fits שמואל. The actual explanation comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אימא' tells us the גמרא will not reject שמואל's rule. Instead, it will read the משנה's words in a new way so that the challenge goes away. The question stays open until the explanation appears.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Say.' This means 'read it this way instead,' and it introduces a new reading of a source.

phrases.english: Say:
phrases.notes: This opens a new reading of the משנה. The rest continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the challenge in Step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading of the משנה (the full explanation follows on the next amud).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the משנה tells the leader to say 'ברכו,' which leaves him out of the group.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה will be read in a way that fits שמואל. The details come next.
